event_shown.rule: among the test-year onsets that the LSTM with river gauge missed 1 day ahead and the LSTM with a perfect weather forecast caught (validation-chosen warning levels), lasting at least 3 days and with a tropical cyclone within 300 km: the one with the highest peak relative to the basin's high-flow level. An illustration picked by rule, not a measure of typical skill.

findings: 611 high-flow events in the test years over the 12 basins (249 last a single day; median length 2 days); 30 began with a tropical cyclone within 500 km (14 within 300 km), 149 others in May-Sep and 432 in Oct-Apr.
'Tomorrow = today', 1 day ahead, all high-flow days, test years: at the high-flow level itself warned 61%, false 39%, CSI 0.44; at the validation-chosen level (x1.10) warned 56%, false 34%, CSI 0.43.
'Tomorrow = today', 1 day ahead, onsets, test years: at the high-flow level itself warned 0%, false n/a, CSI 0.00; at the validation-chosen level (x1.10) warned 0%, false n/a, CSI 0.00.

Random forest, with river gauge, 1 day ahead, all high-flow days, test years: at the high-flow level itself warned 66%, false 33%, CSI 0.50; at the validation-chosen level (x1.10) warned 60%, false 28%, CSI 0.49.

Random forest, with river gauge, 1 day ahead, onsets, test years: at the high-flow level itself warned 18%, false 58%, CSI 0.15; at the validation-chosen level (x1.10) warned 14%, false 54%, CSI 0.12.

LSTM, past weather only (no gauge), 1 day ahead, all high-flow days, test years: at the high-flow level itself warned 49%, false 49%, CSI 0.33 (single seeds: warned 47% to 49%, false 49% to 53%); at the validation-chosen level (x0.95) warned 52%, false 52%, CSI 0.33.

LSTM, past weather only (no gauge), 1 day ahead, onsets, test years: at the high-flow level itself warned 17%, false 83%, CSI 0.09 (single seeds: warned 16% to 19%, false 81% to 84%); at the validation-chosen level (x0.95) warned 19%, false 84%, CSI 0.10.

LSTM, with river gauge, 1 day ahead, all high-flow days, test years: at the high-flow level itself warned 62%, false 32%, CSI 0.48 (single seeds: warned 59% to 63%, false 34% to 35%); at the validation-chosen level (x1.00) warned 62%, false 32%, CSI 0.48.

LSTM, with river gauge, 1 day ahead, onsets, test years: at the high-flow level itself warned 19%, false 59%, CSI 0.15 (single seeds: warned 18% to 18%, false 61% to 67%); at the validation-chosen level (x1.00) warned 19%, false 59%, CSI 0.15.

LSTM, river gauge + perfect weather forecast, 1 day ahead, all high-flow days, test years: at the high-flow level itself warned 81%, false 18%, CSI 0.69 (single seeds: warned 79% to 81%, false 19% to 20%); at the validation-chosen level (x1.00) warned 81%, false 18%, CSI 0.69.

LSTM, river gauge + perfect weather forecast, 1 day ahead, onsets, test years: at the high-flow level itself warned 64%, false 26%, CSI 0.52 (single seeds: warned 62% to 63%, false 27% to 28%); at the validation-chosen level (x1.00) warned 64%, false 26%, CSI 0.52.

Does a lower warning level help? LSTM, with river gauge: the validation years chose x1.00 / x1.05 / x1.05 for 1 / 2 / 3 days ahead (single seeds 1 day ahead: x1.00 to x1.10). On the test years (description only) a level of x0.70 would warn of 39% of the onsets 1 day ahead instead of 19% at the high-flow level itself, with 83% of those warnings false instead of 59% (CSI of onsets 0.13 against 0.15).

Does a lower warning level help? LSTM, past weather only (no gauge): the validation years chose x0.95 / x0.90 / x0.90 for 1 / 2 / 3 days ahead (single seeds 1 day ahead: x0.90 to x1.00). On the test years (description only) a level of x0.70 would warn of 39% of the onsets 1 day ahead instead of 17% at the high-flow level itself, with 89% of those warnings false instead of 83% (CSI of onsets 0.09 against 0.09).

Verdict for LSTM, with river gauge (what could run today with a river gauge), test years at the validation-chosen level: 1 day ahead - all high-flow days CAUTION (3 basins GO, 4 CAUTION, 5 NOT YET), onsets NOT YET (0 GO, 1 CAUTION, 11 NOT YET); 2 days ahead - all high-flow days NOT YET (2 basins GO, 1 CAUTION, 9 NOT YET), onsets NOT YET (0 GO, 0 CAUTION, 12 NOT YET); 3 days ahead - all high-flow days NOT YET (0 basins GO, 2 CAUTION, 10 NOT YET), onsets NOT YET (0 GO, 0 CAUTION, 12 NOT YET). Each single seed gives the same pooled verdict in 6 of the 6 cases.

Verdict for LSTM, past weather only (no gauge) (no river gauge), test years at the validation-chosen level: 1 day ahead - all high-flow days NOT YET (1 basins GO, 3 CAUTION, 8 NOT YET), onsets NOT YET (0 GO, 0 CAUTION, 12 NOT YET); 2 days ahead - all high-flow days NOT YET (0 basins GO, 3 CAUTION, 9 NOT YET), onsets NOT YET (0 GO, 0 CAUTION, 12 NOT YET); 3 days ahead - all high-flow days NOT YET (0 basins GO, 1 CAUTION, 11 NOT YET), onsets NOT YET (0 GO, 0 CAUTION, 12 NOT YET). Each single seed gives the same pooled verdict in 6 of the 6 cases.

Verdict for LSTM, river gauge + perfect weather forecast (the ceiling: river gauge + a perfect weather forecast), test years at the validation-chosen level: 1 day ahead - all high-flow days GO (11 basins GO, 1 CAUTION, 0 NOT YET), onsets CAUTION (2 GO, 9 CAUTION, 1 NOT YET); 2 days ahead - all high-flow days GO (10 basins GO, 2 CAUTION, 0 NOT YET), onsets GO (7 GO, 4 CAUTION, 1 NOT YET); 3 days ahead - all high-flow days GO (7 basins GO, 4 CAUTION, 1 NOT YET), onsets CAUTION (4 GO, 6 CAUTION, 2 NOT YET). Each single seed gives the same pooled verdict in 4 of the 6 cases.

The same rule applied to 'tomorrow = today', 1 day ahead, all high-flow days: CAUTION (CSI 0.43 against 0.48 for the LSTM with river gauge). 951 of the 1562 high-flow days are the second or later day of an event, when the gauge already shows the river is high; on the 611 onsets 'tomorrow = today' warns of 0% and the LSTM with river gauge of 19%.

LSTM, with river gauge, onsets 1 day ahead at the validation-chosen level, by season: Dec-Feb 18% of 218 warned (57% of the warnings false); Mar-May 19% of 188 warned (63% of the warnings false); Jun-Aug 24% of 93 warned (55% of the warnings false); Sep-Nov 16% of 112 warned (59% of the warnings false).

LSTM, river gauge + perfect weather forecast, onsets 1 day ahead at the validation-chosen level, by season: Dec-Feb 71% of 218 warned (25% of the warnings false); Mar-May 65% of 188 warned (25% of the warnings false); Jun-Aug 43% of 93 warned (37% of the warnings false); Sep-Nov 68% of 112 warned (23% of the warnings false).

LSTM, with river gauge, onsets 1 day ahead at the validation-chosen level, by storm type: tropical 43% of 30 warned (41% of the warnings false); warm-season 19% of 149 warned (57% of the warnings false); cool-season 17% of 432 warned (62% of the warnings false).

LSTM, river gauge + perfect weather forecast, onsets 1 day ahead at the validation-chosen level, by storm type: tropical 77% of 30 warned (26% of the warnings false); warm-season 48% of 149 warned (34% of the warnings false); cool-season 69% of 432 warned (24% of the warnings false).

LSTM, with river gauge, onsets 1 day ahead at the validation-chosen level, by share of the two days' rain that the weather table files under the target day: 0-25% 71% of 52 warned (74% of the warnings false); 25-50% 52% of 69 warned (47% of the warnings false); 50-75% 21% of 149 warned (20% of the warnings false); 75-100% 2% of 335 warned (50% of the warnings false); under 1 mm on both days 17% of 6 warned (91% of the warnings false).

LSTM, river gauge + perfect weather forecast, onsets 1 day ahead at the validation-chosen level, by share of the two days' rain that the weather table files under the target day: 0-25% 40% of 52 warned (28% of the warnings false); 25-50% 54% of 69 warned (21% of the warnings false); 50-75% 65% of 149 warned (31% of the warnings false); 75-100% 71% of 335 warned (24% of the warnings false); under 1 mm on both days 17% of 6 warned (80% of the warnings false).

What a perfect weather forecast adds, 1 day ahead (validation-chosen levels): of 611 onsets the LSTM with river gauge caught 114 and missed 497; the LSTM that also reads the target days' weather caught 308 of the missed ones (62%); 189 were missed by both and 29 were caught only without the forecast.

Peak size, 'Tomorrow = today': the forecast made the day before the peak is 40% of the observed peak in the median event (middle half 18% to 72%; 100% of the 611 events are forecast too low; peak on the onset day: median 27%, later: 82%).

Peak size, LSTM, with river gauge: the forecast made the day before the peak is 45% of the observed peak in the median event (middle half 24% to 77%; 89% of the 611 events are forecast too low; peak on the onset day: median 33%, later: 77%).

Peak size, LSTM, river gauge + perfect weather forecast: the forecast made the day before the peak is 84% of the observed peak in the median event (middle half 63% to 105%; 70% of the 611 events are forecast too low; peak on the onset day: median 77%, later: 91%).

By basin, LSTM, with river gauge, share of onsets warned 1 day ahead against basin properties (Spearman rank correlation, 12 basins): basin area +0.65 (p = 0.022); mean slope -0.93 (p < 0.001); baseflow index -0.48 (p = 0.118); mean length of a high-flow event in the test years +0.85 (p < 0.001). 29 of the 48 correlations looked at for this model reach |rho| >= 0.587 (p < 0.05 in a single test); about 2 would by chance alone.

By basin, LSTM, river gauge + perfect weather forecast, share of onsets warned 1 day ahead against basin properties (Spearman rank correlation, 12 basins): basin area -0.13 (p = 0.681); mean slope +0.54 (p = 0.071); baseflow index +0.76 (p = 0.005); mean length of a high-flow event in the test years -0.08 (p = 0.812). 7 of the 48 correlations looked at for this model reach |rho| >= 0.587 (p < 0.05 in a single test); about 2 would by chance alone.
notes: No model was trained here. All counts and rates come from flood.evaluate, flood.flood_scores, flood.contingency and flood.rates; test years 2005-10-01..2014-09-30, pooled = sums of hits, misses and false alarms over the 12 basins.

Warning level: a warning is given when the forecast exceeds m x the basin's high-flow level (95th percentile of the training years). m is one number per model and lead for all 12 basins, chosen on the grid 0.30..1.50 (step 0.05) by the best pooled CSI of all high-flow days in the validation years 2000-2005 ('tuned'); a tie goes to the level closest to 1. 'plain' is m = 1. 'tuned_for_onsets' is a variant in which the validation CSI of onsets chooses m. The test years chose nothing; tradeoff_test is the whole curve on the test years, as a description only.

The level is chosen on 1232 high-flow days of 5 validation years (the 9 test years hold 1562), so the chosen level is itself uncertain: the single LSTM seeds choose their own level (seeds.l*.tuned.trigger_by_seed) and their range is given next to every LSTM score. No chosen level is at the edge of the grid.

The trade-off sweep over warning levels selects the scored days with the same lines as flood.flood_scores and counts them with flood.contingency (27 000 calls of flood.flood_scores would take over a minute); the script asserts that its tables are identical to flood.evaluate at the plain level and to flood.flood_scores at the chosen level.

Onset = a forecast issued while the river was still at or below the high-flow level (flood.flood_scores). 1 day ahead that is exactly the first day of each event; 2 and 3 days ahead it also includes the second and third day of an event, so the number of 'onset' days grows with the lead. 'Tomorrow = today' can warn of an onset only when the warning level is below the high-flow level.

Verdict criteria were fixed before the scores were looked at (verdict.criteria). The pooled verdict weights basins by their number of high-flow days; per-basin verdicts rest on few events (see by_basin.table n_events), so a single event can move a basin across a line.

Event = consecutive test-year days above the high-flow level; a one-day dip below the level ends an event and the next day starts a new one. started_before_test marks an event already running on the first test day (it is in the catalogue but not counted as an onset). 2 events were still running on the last test day (2014-09-30): their length, and their peak if it came later, is cut there.
The 'where and why' tables (failures: by basin, season, storm type, rain timing, peak size) are for forecasts made 1 day ahead only; the skill tables and the verdict cover 1, 2 and 3 days ahead.

Storm type: 'tropical' = a position of the Atlantic best-track record (HURDAT2, 6-hourly, every status including depressions and remnant or extratropical stages) lay within 500 km of the river gauge on the onset day or the 3 days before (UTC dates; the flow day is a local day, a slack the 3-day window absorbs). That is nearness, not proof that the cyclone caused the rain. Otherwise 'warm-season' (onset May-Sep) or 'cool-season' (Oct-Apr) - a stated proxy for thunderstorm rain against frontal rain, not a weather classification. cyclone_within_300km in the CSV shows how many tags survive a tighter radius. For the day-by-day tables every day of an event carries the tag of its onset; days outside events are tagged by the same rule applied to the day itself.

Rain timing, 1 day ahead: rain_share_target_day = basin-mean Daymet rain filed under the target day / (rain filed under the issue day + under the target day); days with under 1 mm in total are a class of their own. The models without a weather forecast read the weather table up to the issue day only, so a high share means the rise came with rain they could not read.

Caution on 'rain of the target day': Daymet files rain by the rain-gauge observers' day, so part of the rain filed under the target day may already have fallen during the issue day (10_rain_timing.py measures this). 'Not yet in the weather table' is therefore exact; 'not yet fallen' would overstate it, and part of the 1-day-ahead gap could be closed without any forecast by rain measured up to the evening of the issue day.

The perfect weather forecast (lstm_wqf) reads the actual weather of the target days: an upper bound that cannot be had in practice. 'Of those caught with a perfect forecast' is therefore the most a real forecast could add, not what it would add.

Small groups: the 30 onsets with a tropical cyclone nearby are few (one onset moves their warned share by about 3 percentage points), and the cyclone tag overlaps with basin type and season, so the storm-type contrast is a description, not a tested difference.
Peak size: forecast for the peak day issued the day before, divided by the observed peak flow; events already running on the first test day are left out.

By basin: Spearman rank correlations over 12 basins. With n = 12, |rho| must reach 0.587 for p < 0.05 in a single test, and 48 correlations are looked at for each model and rule, so a few will pass by chance; basin properties are also tied to each other (the mountain basins are the steep ones with the highest baseflow index). The table can show a pattern worth a hypothesis; it cannot show a cause.

The random forest has one seed (random_state=0), so its seed spread is not known. lstm_<set> is the average forecast of its seeds; its scores can lie outside the range of the single seeds (it tends to give fewer false warnings), so the seed range is given next to every LSTM score.

flood_events.csv: gauge_id is text with a leading zero - read it with dtype=str. <model>_warned_l<k> = the forecast for the onset day issued k days before was above the high-flow level; ..._chosen_level = above the validation-chosen level of that model and lead. river_low_at_issue_l<k> says whether the river was still low when that forecast was issued.
